**Title:** Efficient Task-Agnostic Knowledge Distillation for Compressing Large-Scale Language Models

**Abstract:**
The deployment of large-scale language models (LLMs) is hindered by their substantial computational and memory requirements. This paper introduces a novel task-agnostic knowledge distillation framework designed to compress LLMs without compromising generalization capabilities across diverse downstream tasks. Unlike previous methods that rely on task-specific datasets, our approach leverages a unified, heterogeneous corpus to train a lightweight student model to mimic the output distributions of a large teacher model. We propose a dynamic attention alignment mechanism that preserves critical semantic structures during the distillation process. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves up to 4x inference speedup and 3x memory reduction while maintaining 98% of the original model’s performance. These results highlight the efficacy of task-agnostic distillation as a scalable solution for efficient LLM deployment in resource-constrained environments.

**Title:** TAD-DA: A Data-Augmented Dataset for Tunisian Arabic Dialect Translation with Native Speaker Annotations

**Abstract:**
This paper introduces TAD-DA, a novel resource for Tunisian Arabic dialect (TAD) translation that addresses the scarcity of high-quality parallel corpora. Unlike existing datasets, TAD-DA integrates manually translated comments curated by native speakers, ensuring cultural and linguistic authenticity. To mitigate data sparsity, we employ advanced data augmentation techniques, specifically segmentation at the stop-word level, to expand the training corpus while preserving semantic integrity. We evaluate the dataset’s impact on machine translation performance using BLEU and METEOR scores across various neural architectures. Results demonstrate significant improvements in translation quality compared to baseline models trained on standard datasets. This resource provides a robust foundation for NLP research in low-resource dialectal contexts, offering both human-verified translations and algorithmically augmented data to enhance model generalization and accuracy.

**Title:** Dual-Granularity Hallucination Detection: A Post-Hoc Analysis of Token and Sentence-Level Discrepancies in Neural Sequence Generation

**Abstract:**
Neural sequence generation models frequently produce factual inconsistencies, commonly termed hallucinations. While existing detection methods often focus on a single level of granularity, this study investigates the efficacy of post-hoc techniques across both token- and sentence-levels. We propose a unified framework that integrates local token-level verification with global sentence-level consistency checks. Through extensive experiments on benchmark datasets for summarization and question answering, we demonstrate that combining these granularities significantly improves detection accuracy compared to single-level approaches. Our analysis reveals that token-level methods excel at identifying specific factual errors, while sentence-level techniques better capture broader contextual contradictions. The results highlight the complementary nature of these approaches, offering a robust strategy for enhancing the reliability of generated text in critical applications.
